blocks.text: JERUSALEM — Israeli lawmakers on Tuesday elected a parliament speaker from the camp opposed to caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, marking a first step toward rolling back the legacy of the country’s divisive veteran leader. Sixty-six of the 120 lawmakers voted in favor of Matan Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu. Netanyahu’s Likud party had nominated Ofir Katz as its candidate. He received 52 votes.
